This is a quick guide to adding emoticons to your subverse.

The code to creating emoticons is actually using the same one that is used for spoilers, but instead of hiding text, it just inserts an image in place of it.

Using .md a[href="_______"] we can alter the spoiler code to look for a word or phrase and then place an image at that spot.

For this example, we'll be using the code .md a[href="mad"] for a angry emoticon. Using this we'll continue with the rest of the code.

The Code

First, we decide which image we want to be used and what type of display it will be utilizing.

.md a[href="mad"] {
 background: url(YOUR IMAGE ADDRESS);
 display: inline-block; /* You can choose another type if you wish */

Second, depending on the size of the image, we add padding to accommodate it. We also add extra margin so it won't be cramped next to any words that may be next to it. We also make the cursor change to it's default on hover. Heads Up: Clicking on the image redirects to a broken link. 

 padding: #px #px #px #px;
 margin-left: 3px; /* 3px is a decent distance, but you can change it to what ever you like */
 margin-right: 3px;
 cursor: default;
}

Tips: I'd recommend a size of 20x20px for your image though you can go larger if you wish. You can also make the image expand on hover. I'd also recommend using an image with a transparent background.

Utilizing Emoticons

Since this is using the same code as a spoiler, utilizing it is similar. For a spoiler, the user types this: [](#s "")

For emoticons, the user types this: []( WORD ) with 'WORD' being whatever word or phrase used in .md a[href="___"]

In our example the user would be typing this: []( mad )

Tips: You can have any amount of emoticons you wish, however, I recommend using a sprite sheet to store them on a single address. Go to @shiny's guide or @Nurdoidz's guide for help on sprite sheets.

To see this in action go to the Steven Universe CSS subverse. We already have a list of emoticons in use.
